meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.en: to know how to, to be able to
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know how to, to be able to', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Indeclinable neuter noun borrowed from French 'menu' (detailed list, from Latin 'minutus').

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодняшний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('today's').

examples.trans: The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!

examples.text: С сегодняшнего дня говорите мне только правду.
examples.trans: From today on, tell me only the truth.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'елиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to share', paired with 'делиться'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.trans: I am very curious to know the answer.

examples.text: Как любопытно. И почему мы должны вам подчиняться?
examples.trans: How curious. And why must we obey you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He is so sweet and very sociable!

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Now I have to look for a new job.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least, just', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something, anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешной'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('funny, ridiculous').

examples.text: Ты такой смешной, Тузик! Кто такой сладкий?
examples.trans: You're so funny, Tuzik! Who's so sweet?

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to get out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
